clue.text: Unprofitable attachment in old mother's household

definitions.text: Unprofitable attachment in old mother's household

parts.words: Unprofitable attachment in old mother's household
parts.note: the nursery-rhyme Old Mother Hubbard went to her larder and found it bare, so any fondness for it there could bring no reward

explanation.surface: A sentimental but fruitless bond within an elderly mother's home.
explanation.walkthrough: CUPBOARD LOVE is affection shown only in hope of food or reward; Old Mother Hubbard's cupboard was famously bare, so loving it gets you nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names fondness feigned for gain; in the rhyme's empty larder such self-interested affection would earn no profit at all.

clue.text: Left for South in S American capital to find wild cat

indicators.note: the letter for left takes the place of the letter for south in the city name

parts.note: Caracas is the capital of Venezuela in South America

explanation.surface: A traveller in Venezuela's capital hopes to spot a wild feline.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the final S of CARACAS for L (left) to get the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The caracal is a lynx-like feline of Africa and Asia with tufted black ears.

clue.text: .Make smart coppers surround the border

indicators.note: the coin letters go on either side of the edge, enclosing it

parts.note: coppers are pennies, each abbreviated P
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: Smarten up while police officers ring the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' looks like police but means pennies, P and P, placed round RIM.
explanation.definitionFit: To primp is to groom oneself fussily, tidying hair and clothes.

clue.text: Alice's lot going crazy with swing

indicators.note: letters that go crazy are thrown into disorder and rearranged

parts.note: its letters taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: Alice and her friends get wild on the playground swing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going crazy' rearranges ALICESLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To oscillate is to move to and fro like a pendulum, a synonym of the verb swing.

clue.text: It's used to catch river fish

parts.note: an eel is a snakelike fish

explanation.surface: Describing a tool for landing fish from a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler's reel winds in the line that lands the catch.

clue.text: Evangelist has support of cordial Laodicean

indicators.note: in a down entry the second piece sits beneath the first, holding it up

parts.note: Luke is one of the four Gospel writers
cordial means warm and friendly

explanation.surface: A gospel writer backs a half-hearted citizen of Laodicea.
explanation.walkthrough: The church at Laodicea is condemned in Revelation for being neither hot nor cold, so 'Laodicean' means half-hearted.
explanation.definitionFit: Laodicean describes indifference in religion or politics, the tepid attitude the church was rebuked for.

clue.text: Dickensian taxidermist as space-traveller

explanation.surface: A Dickens character who stuffs animals goes into orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Venus stuffs and articulates bones in Dickens's Our Mutual Friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Venus is the bone-articulator in Our Mutual Friend; a planet is a body journeying endlessly through space.

clue.text: Faced being beheaded. A bit tricky. Give up?

indicators.note: tricky letters are slippery and can be put in a new order
losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: taken as written before losing its opening letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone facing execution finds things tricky and wonders whether to surrender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being beheaded' cuts FACED to ACED; 'tricky' mixes ACED with ABIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to renounce a throne or duty, to surrender it formally.

clue.text: Local tax raised without being paid. it could create an explosion

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the paid letters wrap the tax

parts.note: PD is the abbreviation for paid

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means read upwards, so the tax word runs backwards

parts.note: rates were the old British local property tax

explanation.surface: A council charge goes up without being settled, and tempers may explode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns RATE to ETAR; 'without' places it between P and D. Rates were Britain's local property tax until 1990.
explanation.definitionFit: A petard is a small bomb for blowing open gates, as in hoist with one's own petard.

clue.text: Second chance to see the sport when gunman is attacked on board

definitions.text: Second chance to see the sport

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, are the army's gunners
a chess king under attack on the board is in check

explanation.surface: A fresh opportunity to watch a game after a shooter is set upon on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship, but it is the chessboard. A rain check was a ticket for a later game if rain stopped play.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a ticket letting spectators return when weather stopped a match, now any postponed offer.

clue.text: Peer was one of three in the pound

definitions.text: was one of three in the pound

explanation.surface: A lord who was once a third of a sterling unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The noble was an old English gold coin worth 6s 8d, a third of a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobleman is a member of the peerage; the old gold coin was valued at a third of a pound sterling.

clue.text: Officer holds up a dome

indicators.note: the officer's letters hold the next word inside them

parts.note: Col is short for colonel
taken as written

explanation.surface: A commander raises a domed roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds up' reads as one verb but splits: COL holds UP, then A.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupola is a small rounded roof crowning a building, a type of dome.

clue.text: Gammadion, was it? Ask for reconstruction

indicators.note: letters put up for rebuilding are rearranged into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a symbol was a gammadion and wants it rebuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: A gammadion is a cross made of four Greek capital gammas.
explanation.definitionFit: Gammadion is the technical name for the hooked cross, formed from four gamma shapes.

clue.text: Tether the latter part back round a ram's head

indicators.note: the reversed word goes round the following letters, enclosing them
back means the word for the end piece is read in reverse

parts.note: the tail is the latter part of something

indicators.note: a ram's head is the first letter of that word

explanation.surface: Tying up the back end of an animal around the head of a ram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TAIL to LIAT; 'round' puts A and R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a long rope for picketing or lassoing livestock, used as a tether.

clue.text: Gambling allowed in the course of one's journey

indicators.note: something in the course of a journey falls in its middle

parts.note: a route is the way taken on a journey
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Betting permitted while a traveller is on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino game of chance played on a spinning numbered wheel.

clue.text: Kind of band seen by a road — "army" band?

parts.note: a brass band is a type of band

explanation.surface: A brass ensemble marching beside a road like an army band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'army' band is a pun: a band worn on the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassard is a cloth badge strapped round the upper sleeve, an armlet.

clue.text: Mississippi's capital (so-called) not used in prison construction?

definitions.text: Mississippi's capital (so-called) not used in prison construction?

parts.words: Mississippi's capital (so-called) not used in prison construction?
parts.note: the state capital is Jackson, the Confederate general Jackson's nickname

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Mississippi city's nickname was not used in building jails.
explanation.walkthrough: Jackson, Mississippi shares its name with General Thomas 'Stonewall' Jackson; Lovelace's poem says stone walls do not a prison make.
explanation.definitionFit: The general Jackson's nickname matches the masonry Lovelace said fails to make a jail.

clue.text: Roman priest takes care of the dance

parts.note: a flamen was a priest of one god in ancient Rome
c/o, CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of

explanation.surface: A Roman cleric looks after the dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is the passionate Andalusian gypsy dance with stamping and guitar.

clue.text: Girl's dried fruit everyone rejected

parts.note: a prune is a dried plum

indicators.note: rejected means the word for everyone is turned back

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A girl's prunes were turned down by everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns ALL to LLA. 'Girl's' reads as 'Girl is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prunella is a female given name.

clue.text: Quickly getting right on top in a riot

indicators.note: letters in a riot are in disorder, so they are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting control of a riot fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a riot' rearranges R, ON and TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronto, from Spanish, is informal for at once, without delay.

clue.text: Wind snakes round about

indicators.note: the snakes go round the next word, enclosing it

parts.note: boas are large constricting snakes
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Serpents coil and wind around something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' looks like a verb for the snakes coiling, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Boreas is the Greek god of the north wind.

clue.text: Sportswear for the honest village blacksmith for instance

definitions.text: the honest village blacksmith for instance

explanation.surface: Athletic clothing suits the upright blacksmith of a village.
explanation.walkthrough: Longfellow's The Village Blacksmith says 'his brow is wet with honest sweat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jersey or pullover is athletic garb; Longfellow's smith toils until he perspires honestly.

clue.text: Having finished, send out return of extra work done

parts.note: over means finished

indicators.note: the return of a word sends it back, reading backwards

parts.note: emit means send out

explanation.surface: Done for the day, someone sends back extra work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns EMIT to TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Hours worked beyond the normal schedule.

clue.text: A little honey that jeopardized Jonathan's life

definitions.text: A little honey that jeopardized Jonathan's life

parts.words: A little honey that jeopardized Jonathan's life
parts.note: in 1 Samuel 14 Saul's son ate a scrap of honey against his father's oath and was nearly put to death for it

explanation.surface: A biblical moment when a scrap of honey almost cost Jonathan his life.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan said 'I did but taste a little honey... and, lo, I must die.' A taste is also a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sample of food, like the honey Jonathan sampled against Saul's command.

clue.text: Worker let out Kipling at school

parts.note: a worker bee

indicators.note: out signals the word let is put out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An employee is released, as Kipling was from school.
explanation.walkthrough: Beetle is Kipling's self-portrait in his school stories Stalky & Co.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling based the bespectacled schoolboy in Stalky & Co on himself.

clue.text: Wine given to girl

parts.note: Kay is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A bottle presented to a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian dessert vintage.

clue.text: Due to hear something from Horace

indicators.note: what is heard is a word said aloud, matching another in sound

parts.note: the Roman poet Horace wrote odes

explanation.surface: Expecting to hear a piece by Horace.
explanation.definitionFit: Money owed is payable, outstanding.

clue.text: Yet it used to show the name of Paul's companion

indicators.note: the name is on show inside the run of words

explanation.surface: An old inscription once bore the name of one of St Paul's companions.
explanation.walkthrough: Titus travelled with St Paul and received one of his letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus was a Gentile convert who accompanied Paul and to whom an epistle is addressed.

clue.text: Many guineas won at this card-game

explanation.surface: A gambling card game where a fortune is won.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1,000 and 2,000 Guineas horse races are run at Newmarket, a Suffolk racecourse; it is also a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: The Suffolk racecourse hosts the Guineas classics; it also names a family card game of matching pay-out cards.

clue.text: Enter an actor — one seen in a music centre

definitions.text: one seen in a music centre

parts.note: to enter data is to record it
a player is an actor

explanation.surface: Stage directions bring a performer on at a concert hall.
explanation.walkthrough: A music centre was a hi-fi unit combining turntable, radio and cassette deck.
explanation.definitionFit: The turntable was one component of a combined home stereo unit.
